data.long_meaning: Herod is a name of Greek origin, derived from the Greek word 'herode', meaning 'hero'. The name became popular among the Jews during the Hellenistic period and was borne by several powerful rulers in Judea, including King Herod the Great, who is known for his building projects, particularly the rebuilding of the Second Temple in Jerusalem.

in_english.name: Herrod
in_english.long_meaning: The name Herrod in English is derived from the Greek word 'heros', meaning 'hero'. It is most commonly used to refer to Herod the Great or the Herodian dynasty in general.

data.cultural_impact: The name Herod is significantly associated with the powerful and reigning Romans and Greeks during the Hellenistic and Roman periods in Judea. Herod the Great, a notable bearer of the name, was known for his extensive building projects, including the rebuilding of the Second Temple in Jerusalem, which to this day stands as a testament to the ingenuity and power during that time.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Herod, while of Greek origin, carries a deeper spiritual significance in the context of biblical history. As a Jewish name borne by several rulers in Judea, it is a reminder of the complexity of Jewish history and culture. Herod the Great, specifically, is known for ordering the massacre of the innocent children in Bethlehem in an attempt to kill the newly born King of the Jews, Jesus Christ. This event serves as a poignant reminder of the potential darkness that can lurk in power and authority. Similarly, the name Herod can be seen as a call to maintain a balance between worldly power and spiritual thriving, and to never let worldly ambitions cloud one's true purpose and calling as a follower of Christ.
